source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
New York State has 31 mapped data centers, but only one publishes an IT capacity figure, so the state's AI-relevant power load cannot be read from operator disclosures.

The one facility with a number is CyrusOne's NYM7 in Wappingers Falls, at 3 MW of IT capacity across 100,000 square feet of technical space. That is roughly 30 watts per square foot, a density consistent with enterprise colocation rather than accelerator-dense halls. It carries SSAE 16 Type II certification, which speaks to audited security controls for sensitive workloads, not to power delivery or grid access.

The disclosure gap matters more than the facility. Thirty of the 31 mapped New York facilities publish no power figure, so a single 3 MW campus cannot stand in for the state's capacity, and its nominal rank first in the state is an artifact of who discloses rather than who is largest. The suitability score of 46 out of 100 is computed only from published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion listed as missing.

What the data does not cover is the part that would decide AI placement: grid interconnection, available headroom, cooling specification, and expansion plans. Without those, this campus cannot be assessed as a site for AI workloads, and neither can the 30 New York facilities that publish nothing at all.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
